name: edge-reveal-control
description: Defect 4 CONTROL. Identical to overview-survives-a-hidden-sidebar except the rail is never moved to Overview, so the sidebar is showing an ordinary SPACE when it is hidden. Its only job is to say whether the edge-hover reveal works at all on this build. If this fails too, the reveal is broken independently of the Overview pane and belongs to its own task; if it passes, the pane is what breaks it.

actions.note: first paint, and the sidebar announces itself
the ordinary space sidebar, before it is hidden
collapse the sidebar. cmds-sidebar-collapse proves this chord reaches the app on this build.
graded proof the collapse happened - without this a failed reveal cannot be told from a sidebar that never hid
the left window edge, where the reveal is armed. x=3 rather than 0: the true edge can land outside the window on a retina backing scale.
what the edge hover actually brought back
leave the edge. 500 is clear of both the arming strip and the revealed pane, so the pointer is outside the zone at either of its two widths
the pane animates shut over kSidebarResizeAnimationDuration; this is the same wait the reveal above is given
the strip after the pointer left - this must read like 'hidden', not like 'revealed'

assertions.label: the-edge-hover-brought-the-sidebar-back
assertions.desc: Asserts the strip CHANGED between hidden and revealed, so it is RED while the reveal is broken and goes green when it works. Measured 2026-08-17: delta=0.00 - the hover brought nothing back, on an ordinary SPACE with no Overview involved. That is what makes this the control: the reveal is broken independently of the Overview pane.

assertions.label: leaving-the-edge-hid-it-again
assertions.note: The same region and threshold the reveal is graded on, read in the other direction. A reveal that never closes would leave this delta at 0, which is exactly the reading the reveal itself gave before the fix

assertions.desc: Cmd+Q still quits with the sidebar hidden
